query: How can we reduce declined expense submissions?

per_column.name: missing_source_id
per_column.rationale: Completeness of the submission (providing a source_id) is a settable property of the submission; requiring/supplying it is an intervenable lever that could plausibly affect decline rates.

per_column.name: missing_processed_date
per_column.rationale: Whether a processed_date exists is largely a downstream artifact of the processing/decline outcome itself rather than a prior cause; it is not a settable treatment nor a common cause.

per_column.name: processed_date_dt
per_column.rationale: A parsed timestamp of processing; occurs after submission and is a consequence of the workflow, not an intervenable treatment nor a confounder.

per_column.name: processing_delay_days
per_column.rationale: Processing turnaround time is an operationally controllable lever (staffing, SLAs) that could be set/changed and plausibly affects decline outcomes; intervenable.

per_column.name: is_high_amount
per_column.rationale: Amount can drive both scrutiny/processing behavior (treatment) and decline likelihood; a common cause to adjust for, not named in the query. Derived from original 'amount'.

per_column.name: high_risk_department
per_column.rationale: Department risk profile can influence both how submissions are handled and the likelihood of decline; a plausible common cause not named in the query.

per_column.name: high_risk_category
per_column.rationale: Expense category risk can affect both processing/treatment and decline probability; a plausible confounder not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The query poses an interventional 'how can we reduce declines?' question. At least two added columns are genuinely intervenable treatments: submission completeness (missing_source_id) and processing_delay_days, both settable via policy/operations. Three columns (is_high_amount, high_risk_department, high_risk_category) function as plausible confounders -- common causes of both handling/treatment and the decline outcome -- and none were named or clearly implied in the terse query, demonstrating the capability under test. Some added columns (missing_processed_date, processed_date_dt) are post-outcome artifacts (colliders/consequences) rather than confounders and do not support the causal setup. Overall the set satisfies the what-if claim: an intervenable treatment plus non-query-named confounders, though a few columns are irrelevant mediators/colliders lowering precision.
